messages.subject: SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat Qvalue filtering
parts:
Dear MSstatsTeam

I was wondering, why the SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat importer handles Qvalues differently on ProteinGroup (--> NA) and ElutionGroup (--> 0) level:

INFO  [2023-03-29 15:28:27] ** Intensities with values not smaller than 0.01 in PGQvalue are replaced with NA
INFO  [2023-03-29 15:28:27] ** Intensities with values not smaller than 0.01 in EGQvalue are replaced with 0

Can you explain me the rational behind this approach?

I just did a quick comparison with a recent Spectronaut search and realized, that the median normalization on FeatureLevel is affected by the way the Qvalue is applied:
As you can see from this example, the Qvalue filtering applied by the SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat importer causes issues with the median normalization leading to the overestimation of certain sample groups. If I perform a Qvalue filtering during SpectroNaut export (or in R before SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat), then this effect is not observed...

Here is the code I've used to generate the normalization plot above:

library(MSstats)
library(tidyverse)
library(vroom)


gg_norm_overview <- function(FeatureQuant) {
  #facet labels
  facet_labels <- c("raw input", "normalized (w/o censored values)", "normalized (after imputation)")
  names(facet_labels) <- c("Log2Int","ABUNDANCE","newABUNDANCE")
 
  minval <- if(any(na.omit(FeatureQuant$INTENSITY == 0))){
    0
  } else if (any(is.na(FeatureQuant$INTENSITY)) | any(is.infinite(FeatureQuant$INTENSITY))) {
    min(na.omit(floor(log2(FeatureQuant$INTENSITY[is.finite(FeatureQuant$INTENSITY)]))))
  } else {
    min(log2(FeatureQuant$INTENSITY))
  }
 
  gg_norm_overview <- FeatureQuant %>%
    mutate(Log2Int = log2(INTENSITY)) %>%
    pivot_longer(.,c(Log2Int, ABUNDANCE, newABUNDANCE), names_to = "ABU", values_to = "Log2Intensities") %>%
    mutate(across(ABU, factor, levels=c("Log2Int","ABUNDANCE","newABUNDANCE"))) %>%
    ggplot(., aes(y=Log2Intensities, x=originalRUN, fill=GROUP)) +
    geom_boxplot(alpha=0.7) +
    theme_minimal() +
    facet_wrap(~ ABU, ncol = 1, labeller = labeller(ABU = facet_labels)) +
    ylim(minval, max(na.omit(ceiling(log2(FeatureQuant$INTENSITY))))) +
    theme(legend.position="bottom") +
    labs(fill = "Condition", x = "Run") +
    theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45,hjust=1,size=8))
 
  return(gg_norm_overview)
}


SNexport <- vroom("SNreport.xls")
annotation <- vroom("annotation.csv")

#performing Qvalue prefiltering (PG & EG < 0.01), before MSstatsImport
SNexport_filt <- SNexport %>% filter(PG.Qvalue < 0.01) %>% filter(EG.Qvalue < 0.01)

protnames <- head(unique(SNexport_filt$PG.ProteinAccessions), 100)

#creating subset of only 100 ProteinGroups to speed up processing in this example
SNexport_min <- SNexport[SNexport$PG.ProteinAccessions %in% protnames,]
SNexport_filt_min <- SNexport_filt[SNexport_filt$PG.ProteinAccessions %in% protnames,]

#process unfiltered SpectroNaut data (Qvalue filtering is performed during "SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat" step)
SNimport <- SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat(SNexport_min, annotation)
SNquantData <- dataProcess(SNimport, featureSubset = "topN", n_top_feature = 100, censoredInt = "0")
#remove all entries in "remove" column with value TRUE (originating from topN and other import filtering)
SNFeatQuant <- SNquantData$FeatureLevelData %>% filter(!remove)
gg_norm_overview(SNFeatQuant)

#process pre-filtered SpectroNaut data (PG.Qvalue & EG.Qvalue < 0.01)
SNimport_filt <- SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat(SNexport_filt_min, annotation)
SNquantData_filt <- dataProcess(SNimport_filt, featureSubset = "topN", n_top_feature = 100, censoredInt = "0")
#remove all entries in "remove" column with value TRUE (originating from topN and other import filtering)
SNFeatQuant_filt <- SNquantData_filt$FeatureLevelData %>% filter(!remove)
gg_norm_overview(SNFeatQuant_filt)

I've used R 4.2.3, MSstats 4.7.2 and MSstatsConvert 1.9.3.

You can find the SNexport_min and annotation data frame here.

Thank you for looking into this and explaining the rationale behind your Qvalue filtering approach.

Best,
Christian
